source: User message; clarifications normalized for spelling, response values retained.

proposal.current: OPEN-01/02 in draft v2 already establishes full name and spouse name at every interview/recording.
proposal.proposed: Keep the identity opening as a reusable block, separate from all substantive questions; repeat it for each interview and newly started recording.
proposal.reason: Retain the user-directed opening. No Catholic oath or notarization imported.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Keep the identity opening as a reusable block, separate from all substantive questions; repeat it for each interview and newly started recording.

proposal.current: “What are you asking the council to grant in this case...”
proposal.proposed: What outcome are you seeking, and which specific facts do you want the council to consider in support of it?
proposal.reason: Puts request before discovery and separates applicant claim from council decision. Keep type options in a staff-guided field.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: What outcome are you seeking, and which specific facts do you want the council to consider in support of it?

proposal.current: General first-difficulties / what-happened-next prompts.
proposal.proposed: For each important event, record when it occurred, when you learned about it, and whether the date is exact or approximate.
proposal.reason: Occurrence and discovery dates can differ, especially concealment. One event record, not repeated copies of one question.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: For each important event, record when it occurred, when you learned about it, and whether the date is exact or approximate.

proposal.current: “What did you personally see, hear or experience, and what did you learn from another source?”
proposal.proposed: Describe what you personally know. Identify any information you learned from someone else and how you learned it.
proposal.reason: Clearer source attribution; do not turn the source into a required witness or share the other applicant’s private submission.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Describe what you personally know. Identify any information you learned from someone else and how you learned it.

proposal.current: Existing evidence questions ask connection and provenance, but as separate broad prompts.
proposal.proposed: For each disputed fact, identify the supporting item, its date/source if known, what it shows, and any limitations or conflicting information.
proposal.reason: Tie evidence to a fact rather than collecting unrelated documents. Keep unknowns and allegations distinct.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: For each disputed fact, identify the supporting item, its date/source if known, what it shows, and any limitations or conflicting information.

proposal.current: Two general closing questions.
proposal.proposed: What relevant fact has not yet been covered, and is anything you said today in need of clarification?
proposal.reason: Combine duplicate catch-all prompts into one closing question without a new signature.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: What relevant fact has not yet been covered, and is anything you said today in need of clarification?

proposal.status: Draft begins events without a detailed decision block
proposal.current: Draft SEEK/TIME has general grounds/sequence prompts; no focused courtship decision module.
proposal.proposed: How did you decide to marry, what did each of you understand you were committing to, and what had you discussed before the wedding?
proposal.reason: Factual exploration of that time; no assumption that Catholic nullity criteria determine an Orthodox outcome.

answers.clarification: Organize into explicit topics: Children, Money, Intimacy, etc.
answers.reconciledTreatment: Category-based decision-to-marry discovery, including explicit Children, Money and Intimacy topics.

proposal.current: Pressure is only mentioned in broad follow-up examples.
proposal.proposed: Was there pressure affecting the decision to marry? Identify its source, what happened, when, and how it affected the decision.
proposal.reason: Avoid yes/no-only screening and avoid treating ordinary family involvement as proven coercion.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Was there pressure affecting the decision to marry? Identify its source, what happened, when, and how it affected the decision.

proposal.current: Draft timeline does not specifically ask about doubts discussed before the wedding.
proposal.proposed: Did you have serious reservations before the wedding? What were they, were they discussed, and what happened next?
proposal.reason: Relevant stated facts, not automatic invalidity or a universal requirement to produce witnesses.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Did you have serious reservations before the wedding? What were they, were they discussed, and what happened next?

proposal.current: Draft chronology covers events generally.
proposal.proposed: Did a specific event at or immediately before the ceremony affect your ability or willingness to proceed? Describe the event and what you remember.
proposal.reason: A conditional event question, not a medical diagnosis, broad sexual history or imported canonical test.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Did a specific event at or immediately before the ceremony affect your ability or willingness to proceed? Describe the event and what you remember.

proposal.current: FACT follow-up asks what was represented/not disclosed and discovered later.
proposal.proposed: What fact was represented or withheld, what did you believe before marriage, when did you learn the difference, and what evidence supports that sequence?
proposal.reason: Use a separate claim/evidence block for each alleged concealment; never label it established deception automatically.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: What fact was represented or withheld, what did you believe before marriage, when did you learn the difference, and what evidence supports that sequence?

proposal.current: Draft no dedicated agreement question.
proposal.proposed: Was there a specific agreement, promise or condition important to your decision to marry? What was agreed, by whom, when and how was it understood?
proposal.reason: Neutral facts only; not wholesale import of Catholic simulation, permanence or procreation checkboxes.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Was there a specific agreement, promise or condition important to your decision to marry? What was agreed, by whom, when and how was it understood?

proposal.current: FACT-01–05 are shared but do not specify infidelity timing/source.
proposal.proposed: Describe the alleged unfaithfulness, when it occurred, when you learned of it, your source of knowledge and the supporting evidence.
proposal.reason: Avoid assuming guilt or requiring identifying details unrelated to the council inquiry.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Describe the alleged unfaithfulness, when it occurred, when you learned of it, your source of knowledge and the supporting evidence.

proposal.current: General absence/contact description.
proposal.proposed: When did the separation begin, what contact or support continued, what efforts were made to communicate or reconcile, and which facts about the absence do you know directly?
proposal.reason: Distinguish absence from known intention; do not require the absent spouse’s account or address.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: When did the separation begin, what contact or support continued, what efforts were made to communicate or reconcile, and which facts about the absence do you know directly?

proposal.current: No dedicated incident structure.
proposal.proposed: Describe the relevant incident or pattern, dates or periods, what you experienced directly, and any existing reports or evidence you wish to provide.
proposal.reason: Prefer specific acts to character labels. Do not import foreign reporting procedures, demand unnecessary detail or reopen rejected child testimony.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Describe the relevant incident or pattern, dates or periods, what you experienced directly, and any existing reports or evidence you wish to provide.

proposal.current: Current denomination fields do not explain the alleged change and chronology.
proposal.proposed: What change in religious affiliation or practice is relevant to your request, when did it occur, how do you know, and how did it affect married life?
proposal.reason: Claim and chronology only; avoid equating occasional attendance with a formal finding of leaving the faith.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: What change in religious affiliation or practice is relevant to your request, when did it occur, how do you know, and how did it affect married life?

proposal.current: No structured onset/discovery/course of alleged addiction.
proposal.proposed: Describe the behavior you believe is relevant, when it began or became known, its effect on married life, and any help sought that you can factually describe.
proposal.reason: Do not diagnose the spouse from a checkbox or require universal medical-record release.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Describe the behavior you believe is relevant, when it began or became known, its effect on married life, and any help sought that you can factually describe.

proposal.current: One shared FACT block repeatable by ground.
proposal.proposed: Use one factual block for each selected ground, with event date, discovery date, knowledge source and evidence links; show only the relevant approved follow-up prompts.
proposal.reason: Organize without duplicating the same fact across six questionnaires or creating new grounds.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Use one factual block for each selected ground, with event date, discovery date, knowledge source and evidence links; show only the relevant approved follow-up prompts.

proposal.current: Draft does not require childhood, parents or sibling histories.
proposal.proposed: Is there a specific earlier experience that directly helps explain a fact relevant to this petition? Describe only that connection.
proposal.reason: Adapt common family-background theme into a conditional interview follow-up, not a compulsory lifelong biography.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Is there a specific earlier experience that directly helps explain a fact relevant to this petition? Describe only that connection.

proposal.current: Draft general events only.
proposal.proposed: Were the problems described already evident before marriage, or did they arise later? What did each party know at the time?
proposal.reason: A frequently repeated temporal distinction. Keep absence of knowledge separate from proof of concealment.

sources.locator: PDF p.16, courtship vs married life

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Were the problems described already evident before marriage, or did they arise later? What did each party know at the time?

proposal.current: Draft factual chronology does not explore financial/domestic conflict specifically.
proposal.proposed: If relevant, give a concrete example of how an important financial, household or parenting decision was made and how the disagreement affected the marriage.
proposal.reason: Conditional factual example, not a universal inventory of private spending or a civil custody determination.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: If relevant, give a concrete example of how an important financial, household or parenting decision was made and how the disagreement affected the marriage.

proposal.current: Draft events may not show how issues were raised and addressed.
proposal.proposed: For a relevant disagreement, what was communicated, how did the other party respond, and what action followed?
proposal.reason: Concrete sequence is more useful than judging general communication quality.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Do not add/replace this proposal; preserve prior approved CTM policy.

proposal.current: Draft does not request blanket medical history or release.
proposal.proposed: Where directly relevant to the stated issue, describe any professional help actually sought, its dates if known, and the facts you are authorized and able to provide.
proposal.reason: Keep medical/counseling material conditional and separate from clergy-name-only application field; no automatic third-party contact or records release.

answers.clarification: Proposed idea liked, wording too ambiguous; explicitly identify medical, psychological, etc. Revised wording remains for confirmation.
answers.reconciledTreatment: Draft explicit medical/psychological/psychiatric help wording separately; not finalized just because topic was liked.

proposal.current: No standardized repeated separation/reunion block.
proposal.proposed: For each relevant temporary separation: when, why, for how long and what led to resuming life together? Then record final separation separately.
proposal.reason: Merge repeated source variations into one repeatable block; do not require all dates to be exact.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: For each relevant temporary separation: when, why, for how long and what led to resuming life together? Then record final separation separately.

proposal.current: “What attempts at reconciliation were made, when, and what happened?”
proposal.proposed: Identify each relevant reconciliation attempt, who participated, approximate date and outcome. Separate what you observed from what you were told.
proposal.reason: Retain application priest-name-only requirement; this deeper block is council interview content.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Identify each relevant reconciliation attempt, who participated, approximate date and outcome. Separate what you observed from what you were told.

proposal.destination: CEREMONIES / before and after each event
proposal.current: No separate interview chronology for two ceremonies.
proposal.proposed: Identify the civil and church ceremonies separately. What was known or occurring before each ceremony, between them and after the church marriage?
proposal.reason: Borrow the useful time separation, not the Catholic convalidation process or its legal effects.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Do not add/replace this proposal; preserve prior approved CTM policy.

proposal.current: Earlier version has no prior-marriage supplement distinct from previous applications.
proposal.proposed: For each relevant earlier marriage, identify the spouse, dates, ceremony type, how it ended and any existing church/civil decision reference you know.
proposal.reason: Document history only; no imported ligamen decision, renewed fee, automatic record-prefill or second open case.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Do not add/replace this proposal; preserve prior approved CTM policy.

proposal.status: Not in draft; do not assume required
proposal.current: No required inquiry about ability to consummate or intimate marital difficulties.
proposal.proposed: Only if directly relevant to the petition and the council asks: is there a specific intimate marital difficulty you wish to explain, including when it arose or became known?
proposal.reason: Optional approval of a narrow interview topic, not adoption of Catholic consummation definitions, proof thresholds or a mandatory sexual-history survey.

answers.clarification: Is there a specific intimate marital difficulty you wish to explain, including when it arose or became known?
answers.reconciledTreatment: Use user wording as a narrow intimate-difficulty question; no blanket intimate-history inventory.

proposal.destination: Conditional private interview; not new ground
proposal.current: CTM already collects children; no blanket questions about intentions regarding children before marriage.
proposal.proposed: If relevant, what did you and your spouse actually discuss or agree about having children before marriage, and what later changed or became known?
proposal.reason: User may reject or narrow this topic. Do not import Catholic procreation exclusions, contraception rules or a new nullity ground.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: If relevant, what did you and your spouse actually discuss or agree about having children before marriage, and what later changed or became known?

proposal.status: Appeal form and section already approved
proposal.current: Appeal asks for reason and new information/evidence; interviewer can otherwise repeat original discovery.
proposal.proposed: Which earlier decision or finding are you challenging, what information is new, when did it become available and which earlier point does it affect?
proposal.reason: Use an appeal-only question block, not another full biography. Original proceedings remain read-only and no new deadline is introduced.
proposal.action: Adapt factual-source structure; CTM appeal policy

answers.reconciledTreatment: Do not add/replace this proposal; preserve prior approved CTM policy.

proposal.nature: Optional report; not an applicant interview
proposal.status: New user-requested report concept; not approved form content
proposal.current: Application currently records reconciliation priest names; no standardized priest-report template. Prior general priest/witness interview feature was rejected.
proposal.proposed: Report author: name and parish; which party or parties you know; length and nature of contact; which periods of the relationship you know directly.
proposal.reason: Separate a specifically requested priest report from mandatory witness lists, interviews, logins or case access.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Superseded/enriched by direct priest testimony request: scoped link, identified subject, free-form writing or recording.

proposal.current: No direct-knowledge structure for requested pastoral reports.
proposal.proposed: Describe relevant facts you personally observed, with dates if known. Label information told to you by a party separately from your direct observations.
proposal.reason: The witness samples contribute a source-of-knowledge structure, not a right to view parties’ case material.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: Describe relevant facts you personally observed, with dates if known. Label information told to you by a party separately from your direct observations.

proposal.current: Applicant reconciliation field asks priest name only.
proposal.proposed: Describe relevant non-confessional reconciliation assistance you provided, approximate dates and observed outcome. State any limits on what you can report.
proposal.reason: Do not request sacramental confession content or imply a blanket authorization to release pastoral/private information.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Relevant non-confessional assistance only; preserve author and limits of knowledge.

proposal.current: The Catholic samples sometimes ask clergy to assess sincerity or case viability.
proposal.proposed: If you offer an observation or recommendation, identify it as your opinion and state the facts on which it is based; do not make the council decision for it.
proposal.reason: Prefer evidence-grounded observations to a broad character/sincerity score or copied canonical conclusion.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Accept the proposal within its stated scope: If you offer an observation or recommendation, identify it as your opinion and state the facts on which it is based; do not make the council decision for it.

proposal.current: No separate priest report author/date attestation is implemented.
proposal.proposed: At the end of a requested report, record the author, date and signature or authenticated submission method, preserving the exact submitted version.
proposal.reason: Approval chooses the data requirement only. Do not copy Catholic oath/notary/parish-seal rules or create a priest portal without a separate decision.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Author/date/authenticated submission record accepted; signature/link-authentication mechanics not yet finalized.

proposal.status: One draft template with common questions and informal ground prompts
proposal.current: Current draft INT-APPLICANT revision 2 is a single document.
proposal.proposed: Use one common factual core plus only the relevant approved modules: annulment inquiry, selected divorce grounds, multiple ceremonies, prior marriages or appeal; keep a requested priest report as a separate template.
proposal.reason: Avoid copying the same questions into every template. Council controls the process/type; applicant selection is not a decree. No Catholic process categories are imported.

answers.reconciledTreatment: Use common core plus selected accepted categories. Exclude rejected QT22/26/27/30 despite their appearance in the original routing proposal.

generalNotes: Category-based interview/report assembly and link-based priest free-form testimony specified separately in decision register.
